bullets.title: Q2 earnings season setup: estimates revised up 3.4%, strongest in years; 20%+ EPS growth expected
bullets.body: JPM notes Q2 earnings estimates were revised up 3.4% during the quarter vs. a -2% five-year average and -2.7% ten-year average. Revenue growth tracking +12.2% and EPS +23.3% YoY, with Tech/Energy/Communications leading. Markets are shifting focus to earnings season with AI-driven growth expected to sustain elevated valuations. Bank earnings kick off 7/14-7/15, with major tech names (NFLX 7/16, TSMC 7/16) to follow.

bullets.title: META AI monetization inflection: capex plan, frontier model, and API pricing reignite bull case
bullets.body: META surged ~10% after announcing plans to double compute capacity to 14GW by 2027 (~$210-250B capex), launching Muse Spark 1.1 (competitive with Opus 4.6 at ~25% of cost), and beginning to charge via the Meta Model API. JPM Tech Sketch and Jefferies both flagged this as a credible AI monetization pivot; SemiAnalysis was cited as particularly constructive. META is approaching its first close above the 200-day moving average since April; KeyBanc raised PT to $790 (bull case $1,065 at 25x 2028E P/E).

bullets.title: Semis rip on AI capex momentum; memory prices could more than double again in 2027
bullets.body: The semi complex rallied on the META compute expansion and AMAT demand commentary, with SNDK, STX/WDC, ARM, MRVL bouncing from 50-day MAs; optical names NOK +8%, LITE +11%, GLW/CIEN +5%. Jefferies notes HBM prices could more than double in 2027 driven by NVDA Rubin demand; memory prices already up ~4x in this cycle. Taiwan semiconductor exports surged 33% YoY in June, with H1 2026 up 43.9% to $133B; DRAM exports alone +158.5%.

bullets.title: NVDA NDR: accelerating growth with diversified demand; memory shortage to persist for years
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports NVDA management highlighted three growth drivers: AI labs (20% of demand, rising NVDA exposure), hyperscalers (50% of revenue), and neoclouds/enterprise/sovereign (growing fastest). NVDA maintains $20B CPU target and sees SAM expanding via networking. NVDA VP noted compute costs now exceed employee salary costs at the company, underscoring the AI infrastructure spending surge. Memory shortage expected to persist for several years per NVDA.

bullets.title: TSMC CoWoS capacity upgraded; AI packaging gap widens to ~20% on agentic CPU demand
bullets.body: JPM raises TSMC FY26/27/28 CoWoS capacity estimates by 1%/9%/11% to 115k/190k/225k wfpm on strong NVDA and AWS demand. TSMC is accelerating AP7 Phase 2 expansion with 50-60% allocated to CoWoS vs 100% SoIC prior. The demand-supply gap for advanced packaging expanded to ~20% from agentic AI CPU demand surge. TSMC earnings on July 16 are seen as a critical macro catalyst for the semis complex.

bullets.title: US CPI preview: Goldman expects +0.17% core; PSC Macro sees energy deflation offsetting tariff lift
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs expects core CPI +0.17% m/m in June, well below the +0.3% consensus. PSC Macro projects headline -0.1% m/m and core +0.2% m/m, driven by a ~10% MoM gasoline decline and rolling over airfares, with rent disinflation persisting through end-2027. AI-related inflation could add 20-50bps to core PCE by year-end (Goldman AM). Key data next week: US CPI, followed by China GDP and NFLX/TSMC earnings.

bullets.title: September rate hike odds jump to ~67% on market re-pricing; 30Y Treasury hits 5.058%
bullets.body: Market-implied probability of a September FOMC rate hike has risen to approximately 67% per one source (vs. Polymarket at 57% no-change). The 30-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.058%, the highest since the pre-GFC era. Hedgeye notes UST 2Y yield failed at the 4.23% inflation cycle high, and sees a buying opportunity in bonds and equity bond proxies. NASDAQ 100 VIX premium to S&P 500 VIX is at a 20-year high.

bullets.title: Jefferies China AI capex raised 23% to $1T through 2030; Huawei 8K-GPU server launches at WAIC July 17
bullets.body: Jefferies raises 2026-30E cumulative China AI capex by 23% to $1 trillion with power demand +31% to 34GW. China approved 400K H200 chips (vs. 200K US-licensed). Huawei will announce an 8,192-GPU super-node server at WAIC (July 17-20) vs. its current 384-GPU model; Ascend 950 die shrinks boost chips-per-wafer from 74 to 137. TSMC's July 16 earnings are key: strong AI demand signals rally the complex; inventory adjustment signals risk a peak-AI read.

bullets.title: US-Iran tensions: Hormuz governance dispute (Paragraph 5) unresolved; oil falls on contained-risk read
bullets.body: Three commercial vessels were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz; US struck Iranian military infrastructure in response; Iran retaliated against US bases in Bahrain and Kuwait. The core dispute is Paragraph 5 of the MOU—Washington seeks open navigation, Iran seeks governance recognition. Oil has not returned to crisis highs as physical flows adapted. WTI consolidated near $72 as diplomacy (Pakistan, Qatar, Oman) continues. IEA cut 2026 oil demand by 70k bpd but raised supply outlook by 210k bpd; UAE production hit a record 4.1M bpd.

bullets.title: Japan PPI surges 7.1% YoY (fastest since 2023); JGB yields fall 10bp on GPIF domestic asset push
bullets.body: Japan's June domestic CGPI rose 7.1% YoY and 0.4% MoM, both above BOJ forecasts, supporting the case for further BOJ hikes. However, JGB yields fell ~10bp across the curve as Finance Minister Katayama announced measures to push GPIF and households toward domestic Japanese financial assets, supporting yen strength (USD/JPY -0.5%). The yen rally and JGB bid represent a cross-asset shift worth watching for risk-appetite implications.

bullets.title: 2Q ad spend accelerated to +7.7-8.4% YoY; 3Q outlook raised on World Cup, AI-driven targeting
bullets.body: Multiple sources (Piper, Citi) confirm 2Q26 ad spend grew 7.7-8.4% YoY, 80-90bps above expectations, accelerating ~40bps from Q1. World Cup contributed ~200bps. FY26 ad growth outlook raised to 7.8% from 7.6%. Google Search CTRs rose +2.65% YoY in 2Q (vs +1.4% in 1Q) via AI-Max/PMax. Meta ad demand improved throughout the quarter with WhatsApp and Creative catalysts. 3Q projected at +7.8% YoY.

bullets.title: Tech sector led equity inflows at $18.8B; S&P 500 holding 50-day MA; momentum factor reversal
bullets.body: Tech sector led equity inflows with $18.8B in the week ended 7/8. S&P 500 is holding at the 50-day moving average. The momentum factor suffered a 12% drawdown before reversing 3.5% higher over two days; the pullback is attributed to positioning, not fundamentals. AAII bull-bear spread improved to -0.9% from -10.9%. Mag7 is trading near 10-year lows vs SPX. Carry trades are at their most favorable conditions since the dot-com era.

bullets.title: Micron raises US investment to $250B through 2035; pours first NY fab concrete
bullets.body: Micron increased FY2026E net capex to $27B+ and anticipates FY2027E capex of $45B+, with >$250B in planned US fab investment through 2035. The company officially poured concrete for its first New York fab in Clay, NY. Multiple sources note Micron may earn more in 2026 than in the prior 35 years combined. Commerce Secretary is pressing SK Hynix and Samsung to similarly boost US memory output.

bullets.title: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in largest-ever foreign company US listing; leveraged ETFs to follow
bullets.body: SK Hynix priced its US ADR listing at $149/share, raising $26.5B (revised down from $43T to $40T won). This is the largest-ever first-time US listing by a foreign company. Leveraged single-stock SK Hynix ETFs (ticker SKHY, trading SKHYV temporarily) are expected to begin trading Tuesday. The listing triggered a rally in Asian chip stocks including Samsung +4% and KOSPI +3%.

bullets.title: META faces EU DSA breach finding and potential $1.4T teen mental health penalty
bullets.body: The EU Commission preliminarily found Instagram and Facebook addictive design in breach of the Digital Services Act, with a potential fine capped at 6% of worldwide annual revenue. Separately, META faces a $1.4T penalty calculation by state AGs in a teen mental health case—a sum equal to the company's market cap. China also ordered META to reverse its $2B Manus acquisition; Tencent is in talks to become Manus's largest shareholder.

bullets.title: OpenAI and Google selling AI models to Singapore units of Pentagon-blacklisted Chinese tech firms
bullets.body: FT reports OpenAI and Google are selling advanced AI models to Singapore-based subsidiaries of Alibaba, Baidu, and Tencent, despite these firms being on Pentagon blacklists. The three companies are coordinating through the Frontier Model Forum to detect adversarial distillation attempts. China AI LLM stocks Zhipu and MiniMax fell 10-20% on lock-up expiration and new fundraising.

bullets.title: Hedgeye turns bearish oil/energy; sees VIX < 19 as complacent; immediate-term S&P range 7353-7605
bullets.body: Hedgeye is short oil (USO), energy (XOP), and Norway; long airlines (JETS). VIX below 19 with low-end risk range at 14.90; 1-month realized vol set to break below 3-month. QQQ implied vol trading at -11% discount to 30-day realized. S&P 500 immediate-term risk range: 7353-7605; UST 10Y yield range: 4.35-4.57%. Utilities (XLU) and Healthcare (XLV) purchased on weakness.

bullets.title: H2 2026 policy calendar: tariff regime reconstruction, crypto bill, defense funding, midterms
bullets.body: Wolfe DC Policy catalogs key H2 2026 catalysts: Trump reconstructing country-level tariffs post-SCOTUS IEEPA ruling; Section 232 investigations completed on medtech, polysilicon, drones, and robotics. Legislative windows in July, September, and year-end for defense funding, crypto market structure (CLARITY Act needs 60 Senate votes), and China restrictions. Government funding deadline October 1; US-Iran MOU 60-day deadline in August; midterm elections November 3 are a key risk anchor.

bullets.title: AI-related inflation adding 20bp to US core PCE now; could hit 50bp by year-end from memory/software/power
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs AM estimates AI-related price increases (memory, software, electricity) are currently adding 20+ basis points to US core PCE, with a potential 50bp impact by year-end. This inflation dynamic is largely a US phenomenon, with only 8-11bp impact across other developed markets. Global fuel prices remain elevated above $200/bbl equivalent despite crude pullback, as Russia/Middle East outages sustain elevated refining margins.

bullets.title: Regional banks (KRE) up ~15% this quarter; steeper yield curve, benign credit sustaining outperformance
bullets.body: 22V Research notes KRE is up ~15% this quarter on strong loan growth, benign credit, capital markets activity, and a steeper yield curve. EWBC and WTFC are favored with raised price targets. Key risk: if PCE prints hot and the Fed pivots to actual rate hikes, bank sector momentum could stall. Major bank earnings 7/14-7/15 are the next catalyst, with Barclays expecting Equities +21% YoY, FICC +7% YoY, and IB Fees +24% YoY.
